st.headline: US Treasury intervenes to support yen after Japan steps in: Financial Times
st.teaser: The reported action would be the US Treasury’s first direct support for the yen since 2011.
fullText: NEW YORK – The United States Treasury bought yen on July 31 to support the battered Japanese currency , the Financial Times (FT) reported, marking Washington’s first intervention along with Tokyo to support Japan’s currency in more than a decade as it languishes near 40-year lows.
The Federal Reserve Bank of New York conducted a sale of euros to buy yen on behalf of the Treasury through Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the FT said, citing people familiar with the matter.
The report did not indicate any amounts of yen purchased.

Earlier on July 31, the US Treasury informed a number of banks that it might intervene in the yen market and that they should “stand ready for future action”, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.
A Reuters photo of US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s notepad during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David in Maryland showed the words: “To Do” followed by “Buy Japanese Yen (JPY) $5-10 bil”.
The Treasury did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the FT report and the Bessent notepad photo.
The New York Fed and Morgan Stanley also did not immediately respond to request for comment outside regular business hours.
The US last directly supported the yen in 2011, coordinating with fellow Group of Seven nations to stabilise markets after Japan’s earthquake and tsunami disaster.
News of the potential intervention by the Treasury helped boost the yen, with a notable jump during late afternoon trading.
Data from LSEG showed that the US dollar dropped to about 157.6 yen just before 5pm EDT (5am on Aug 1, Singapore time) from about 158.9 yen around 4.14pm EDT .
The US currency had risen in recent weeks to nearly 164 yen, its highest since 1986.
Japan may have sold as much as US$58.97 billion to buy yen on July 30, central bank data indicated on July 31, signalling repeated efforts to stem the yen’s weakness.
Tokyo intervened again in New York trading hours on July 31 , the Nikkei reported on Aug 1 .

Finance Ministry officials could not immediately be reached for comment outside working hours. But the ministry, in an apparent effort to soothe market worries about the limits of Japan’s firepower for large-scale intervention, posted on X that Japan’s monetary authorities have “a broad range of tools to address market liquidity needs”.

“We remain prepared to use available tools as necessary to support orderly market functioning”, including potential access to the Federal Reserve’s standing Foreign and International Monetary Authorities (FIMA) Repo Facility, the ministry said.

The FIMA repo facility, introduced in 2020 to steady markets during the Covid-19 pandemic, allows Japan to raise dollar liquidity without outright sales of US Treasuries, potentially easing funding pressures on Tokyo for intervention. REUTERS

cna.headline: Dogs allowed: Animal hospital opens doors to Japan quake survivors and their pets
cna.teaser: Ryunosuke Animal Hospital in downtown Kumamoto, which was jolted by a powerful earthquake this week, has converted a space into temporary housing for evacuees, with separate rooms for owners of cats and dogs.
fullText: KUMAMOTO, Japan: When a powerful earthquake jolted southern Japan this week, rattling homes and knocking out water and electricity, Tomoko Takaoka bundled up her beloved fluffy dogs and went in search of a safe place to stay.

Unable to reach her parents, Takaoka, a 31-year-old factory worker, turned to a nearby evacuation centre only to discover that her chihuahua, "Ku", and chihuahua-poodle mix, "Sheri", were not welcome.
Faced with the choice of sheltering without them or staying together, she chose the latter, spending the first sweltering night crammed into her car with her canine family.

Eventually, social media posts led her to Ryunosuke Animal Hospital in downtown Kumamoto, which had converted classrooms in its veterinary nurse training school into temporary housing for evacuees, with separate rooms for owners of cats and dogs.
"They worry about fleas, odours, allergies, and noise. Pets are often viewed negatively, which is why many evacuation shelters often don’t allow people and pets to stay together," he added.
The hospital learned that lesson the hard way after the devastating Kumamoto earthquake in 2016. Since then, it has made a point of opening its doors to evacuees with pets whenever disaster strikes.
Its doors immediately opened again after Tuesday's quake, which has claimed at least 36 lives and left thousands without power and running water, although services are slowly being restored.
Clutching Ku and Sheri inside a tent set up at the hospital, Takaoka was among 26 evacuees and their pets sheltering there when Reuters visited earlier this week.
Her dogs occasionally get excited when they encounter new “friends” in the shelter’s designated dog room, Takaoka said, but she does her best to calm them.
She hopes she can return home soon, but more than anything, she's just happy they are together.
"They're just like family to me. I'd like to stay with them as much as possible," she said.

listening.title: Singapore Steps Up Efforts to Cool Urban Heat
listening.transcript: As temperatures rise globally, Singapore is intensifying its urban greening initiatives to combat the 'urban heat island' effect. The Housing and Development Board is introducing cool paints for residential blocks and expanding rooftop gardens in mature estates. Authorities hope these measures will significantly lower ambient temperatures in public residential areas while reducing the reliance on air-conditioning. If successful, these eco-friendly initiatives could serve as a blueprint for other tropical cities facing climate pressures.

economistArticle.title: Oil prices remain highly flammable
paras: The global energy market is once again on a knife-edge. Recent escalations in the Middle East have sent shivers through oil trading desks, threatening to disrupt critical shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts warn that any direct hit on production infrastructure could instantly propel crude prices past the dreaded triple-digit mark.

This precarious situation comes at a delicate time for the global economy. Central banks are painstakingly orchestrating a soft landing, seeking to tame inflation without triggering deep recessions. A sudden, sustained spike in energy costs would immediately disrupt this calculus, reviving the spectre of stagflation that haunted policymakers in previous decades.

For net energy importers, the geopolitical friction acts as an unwelcome tax on growth. In Asian manufacturing hubs, where reliance on imported crude remains stubbornly high, rising input costs threaten to squeeze corporate margins and erode consumer purchasing power. Governments are already contemplating interventions, from direct fuel subsidies to accelerated shifts toward alternative energy.

Meanwhile, OPEC+ cartel members find themselves walking a tightrope. While higher revenues bolster domestic budgets, they are painfully aware that excessive prices destroy demand by forcing consumers to adopt efficiency measures and electric vehicles faster. Striking the right balance between near-term windfalls and long-term market stability has never been more challenging.

Ultimately, the current volatility underscores a deeper structural vulnerability in the global transition. Despite massive investments in renewables, fossil fuels continue to serve as the bedrock of global logistics and heavy industry. Until storage technology and clean capacity can fully match baseline demands, the world remains hostage to the volatile geopolitics of oil-producing states.
economistArticle.cn:
全球能源市场再次处于千钧一发的时刻。中东地区局势的最新升级令石油交易商不寒而栗，威胁到霍尔木兹海峡关键航道的安全。分析人士警告称，对生产基础设施的任何直接打击都可能瞬间将原油价格推高至令人担忧的三位数大关。

这种不稳定的局势发生在全球经济的敏感时期。各国央行正在精心谋划一次软着陆，试图在不引发深度衰退的情况下抑制通胀。能源成本的突然且持续飙升将立即打乱这一计划，使几十年前困扰决策者的滞胀幽灵卷来。

对于能源净进口国而言，地缘政治摩擦无异于对经济增长征收了一项不受欢迎的税。在对进口原油依赖度居高不下的亚洲制造业中心，不断上升的投入成本有可能挤压企业利润并削弱消费者的购买力。各国政府已经开始考虑干预措施，从直接燃料补贴到加速向替代能源转型。

与此同时，欧佩克+（OPEC+）卡特尔成员国发现自己正处于两难境地。虽然更高的收入充实了国内预算，但他们也痛苦地意识到，过高的价格会通过迫使消费者更快地采取节能措施和使用电动汽车来扼杀需求。在短期暴利与长期市场稳定之间取得适当的平衡从未像现在这样具有挑战性。

归根结底，当前的波动凸显了全球转型中更深层次的结构性脆弱性。尽管对可再生能源进行了巨额投资，但化化石燃料仍然是全球物流和重工业的基石。在储能技术和清洁能源产能能够完全满足基线需求之前，世界仍将受制于产油国动荡的地缘政治。

gems.s: A sudden, sustained spike in energy costs would immediately disrupt this calculus, reviving the spectre of stagflation that haunted policymakers in previous decades.
gems.why: This sentence uses vivid metaphors like 'disrupt this calculus' and 'reviving the spectre' to make economic analysis feel dramatic and engaging. 该句运用了“打乱这一考量”和“重燃幽灵”等生动的比喻，使经济分析显得引人入胜且充满张力。

gems.s: Striking the right balance between near-term windfalls and long-term market stability has never been more challenging.
gems.why: This sentence employs the gerund phrase 'Striking the right balance' as a subject, presenting a sophisticated structure typical of formal journalistic writing. 该句使用动名词短语“在……之间取得适当的平衡”作为主语，展现了正式新闻写作中典型的复杂句式。
